Theme

Clothes & getting dressed

pleated adjective

also pleat, pleats

Renaissance

M-O s.v. pleated, ruffled: Vives, collāre rūgātum, a pleated collar
Plin. NH 9.102: testae rūgātae, ridged shells (Lewis & Short s.v. rūgō)

rūgātus, rūgāta, rūgātum

declension

pleated, ruffled (of a garment)

The participle of rūgō, crease: Plautus says of a cloak vidē palliolum ut rūgat, see how it creases (Cas. 2.3.30, Lewis & Short), and the folds of a garment are rūgae (Plin. NH 35.56, Lewis & Short s.v. rūga). We have found no classical instance of rūgātus of a garment; Vives uses it so.

Other words

  • undulātus, undulāta, undulātum — wavy, with a wave-like pattern

    declension · avoid · modern · Varr. ap. Non. 189.26: togae undulātae (Lewis & Short); Traupman 117

    Traupman’s word for pleated, but Lewis & Short has only “diversified as with waves, like watered stuffs”: Varro’s togae undulātae had a wavy pattern, not folds.

SourcesLewis & Short: rugo · Lewis & Short: ruga

Lewis & Short: undulatus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. pleated, ruffled; pleat, ruffle.

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 117.
